task: Repair the existing Template Factory golden visual comparison so a small but locally severe rendered regression cannot pass merely because the full-page mismatch ratio stays below the global threshold.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The Template Factory golden gate currently decides visual equality only from one full-page pixel mismatch ratio. A small rendered element can change materially, including a strong color mutation, while the page-wide ratio remains below 0.005 and the gate incorrectly stays green.
observableOutcomes: The existing full-page maxPixelMismatchRatio remains enforced unchanged.
A second local-severity proof detects concentrated mismatch regions using the same pixel diff evidence.
The canonical stress mutation #35e9ff to #ff0000 over a small rendered region fails locally while remaining below the global 0.005 ratio.
Browser-case evidence records global and local mismatch measurements so a failure is diagnosable rather than threshold-opaque.
unresolvedRisks: A local detector can become oversensitive to anti-aliasing or scattered font-render differences if it ignores pixelmatch filtering.
A fixed grid can split a regression across tile boundaries and create another false negative.
Changing the golden algorithm must invalidate reusable browser evidence through the existing Factory engine fingerprint.

in: Local concentrated mismatch analysis derived from pixelmatch diff output.
Deterministic adversarial self-test for a globally-small, locally-severe color mutation.
out: Golden baseline promotion or Product Owner approval policy.
Template design, screenshots, or golden baseline content.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Golden proof is release-blocking visual evidence and the stress demonstrated a material false negative. The proportionate fix is a deterministic dual global/local detector using the same perceptual pixelmatch evidence, boundary-shifted local windows, explicit minimum mismatch pixels, and adversarial synthetic proof without adding a second visual gate.

acceptanceCriteria: A case passes only when both the existing global mismatch threshold and the new local-severity threshold pass.
Local severity is calculated from pixelmatch-filtered mismatch pixels, not raw RGB inequality.
Local windows are evaluated at multiple offsets so a concentrated regression cannot evade detection by crossing a fixed grid boundary.
The synthetic #35e9ff to #ff0000 mutation proves globalPassed=true, localPassed=false and final status=fail.
The local severity algorithm is a dependency-free shared Factory proof helper, while browser/image dependencies remain confined to the browser quality workflow.
The dependency-free golden semantics helper has an explicit typed ESM declaration contract; TypeScript does not rely on implicit any or suppression.
invariants: Anti-aliasing exclusion and pixelmatch perceptual threshold remain unchanged.
Missing baselines and dimension mismatches retain their current fail-closed behavior.
No golden baseline files are updated by this transaction.

failureModes: A small colored component changes completely but global mismatch stays below 0.005.
A regression straddles a local grid boundary and each fixed tile appears below threshold.
Scattered anti-aliased text pixels create a false local severe region.
Browser evidence reuse ignores a changed golden algorithm.
edgeCases: Image dimensions are smaller than the configured local window.
Mismatch pixel count is below the local minimum evidence floor.
Regression is globally large and should fail regardless of local score.

alternatives.summary: Retain the full-page threshold and add shifted local-window severity over the same pixelmatch mask.
alternatives.reason: This directly closes the proven false-negative class while preserving existing global behavior and perceptual filtering.

alternatives.summary: Lower maxPixelMismatchRatio until the known small color mutation happens to fail.
alternatives.reason: That is blind tuning, increases full-page noise sensitivity, and does not model why a concentrated local regression is important.

alternatives.summary: Require DOM component bounding boxes and compare each component screenshot separately.
alternatives.reason: It would significantly expand browser instrumentation and component identity coupling when shifted local regions can close the proven defect inside the existing screenshot authority.

specialistReviews.finding: The visual authority should remain one golden comparator, not a parallel component-screenshot gate.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extend compareGolden with local semantics and keep one acceptance status.

specialistReviews.finding: A globally tiny change can still be visually dominant if concentrated in a button, badge, swatch, or other focal region.
specialistReviews.resolution: Measure local density with shifted windows and a mismatch-pixel floor instead of relying only on page-wide area.

specialistReviews.finding: Browser proof already produces one stable PNG per page/viewport and pixelmatch excludes anti-aliasing.
specialistReviews.resolution: Reuse the existing screenshot and diff mask; do not add extra browser captures or runtime routes.

specialistReviews.finding: The proven defect is a false-negative class, not a one-off color constant.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add a synthetic adversarial regression where global proof passes and local proof must fail.

challenge.scenario: A 24x24 focal element changes color on a 512x512 screenshot.
challenge.finding: Global mismatch can remain below 0.005 despite a complete local mutation.
challenge.resolution: Require local mismatch density above threshold with a minimum mismatch-pixel floor.

challenge.scenario: The changed element lies across a 64px tile boundary.
challenge.finding: A single fixed grid can split the mismatch and dilute both regions.
challenge.resolution: Evaluate the same local windows with zero and half-window offsets on both axes.

challenge.scenario: Font anti-aliasing produces sparse changed pixels.
challenge.finding: Raw RGB comparison could overreact to rendering noise.
challenge.resolution: Derive local counts only from pixelmatch mismatch output with includeAA=false and threshold 0.1.

challenge.scenario: Only a handful of pixels differ in one window.
challenge.finding: High ratio in a clipped tiny edge window can be misleading.
challenge.resolution: Require an absolute minimum mismatch pixel count before local failure can trigger.

challenge.scenario: The full page exceeds 0.005 but local regions do not.
challenge.finding: Local proof must not weaken the existing global fail condition.
challenge.resolution: Final status is pass only when both globalPassed and localPassed are true.

challenge.scenario: The algorithm changes but prior browser evidence is reused.
challenge.finding: Old cases could retain semantics from the weaker comparator.
challenge.resolution: The existing factoryEngineHash includes template-factory-quality-gate.mjs, invalidating reuse when the comparator changes.

challenge.scenario: A baseline is missing or dimensions differ.
challenge.finding: Local calculation could accidentally hide an existing hard failure.
challenge.resolution: Return the existing missing/dimension-mismatch status before local evaluation.

challenge.scenario: The regression test simply lowers the global threshold.
challenge.finding: The original semantic defect would remain and the test would encode tuning rather than local significance.
challenge.resolution: The stress asserts globalPassed=true and localPassed=false simultaneously.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on the plan-only commit before changing compareGolden.
Add a deterministic CLI/self-test that constructs same-size PNGs with a small #35e9ff to #ff0000 region and proves globalPassed=true/localPassed=false/final fail.
Regression-test that maxPixelMismatchRatio remains .005 in accepted/candidate manifests.
Run exact-head Quality Tests, TypeScript, Production Build and Template Factory Quality Gate v2.
Require Completion Truth and the standard two-phase CLOSE→LEARN lifecycle.

requirements.requirement: Golden proof blocks both globally excessive mismatch and locally concentrated severe mismatch using the same perceptual diff evidence.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A globally-small but locally-severe rendered mutation may not return golden status pass.

requirements.requirement: The existing full-page 0.005 threshold and missing/dimension mismatch behavior remain unchanged while local proof is additive.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The repair may not lower or bypass the canonical global threshold to manufacture the stress result.

requirements.requirement: The exact implementation head passes TypeScript, production build and the relevant Template Factory quality workflow.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The comparator repair must not introduce TypeScript or production build regressions.

notes: Targeted golden false-negative repair only. Handoff evidence flow and shipping/payment are separate transactions. No golden baseline update, no threshold lowering, no parallel visual gate. Plan projection reconciled to Builder/Storefront golden authority: full Known Failure replay, canonical 10-item negative knowledge set, no storefront-ui/quality-knowledge subsystem claim. Local golden semantics were extracted into the existing scripts/lib Shoperation quality-infrastructure namespace so full-repository Quality tests do not require Playwright/pngjs; the real browser comparator consumes the same helper.
